extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, attorneys subject to USPTO discipline, OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing imposition of reciprocal discipline by the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including the notice/response process and the underlying state-bar misconduct grounds that may trigger discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Acting Director of the USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by a duly constituted authority of a State pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order must be served (here by certified mail). The Notice provides the respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more reasons in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). If respondent fails to file a response, the Office may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and impose reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition of reprimand for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reprimand may be ordered under USPTO rules when discipline is predicated upon a public reprimand imposed by a State (cited here as 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order here determines reprimand is the appropriate discipline where the state imposed a public reprimand and the respondent did not timely oppose reciprocal discipline. The Order directs formal reprimand and publication of the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized practice of law — SCR 20:5.5(a)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in the unauthorized practice of law (e.g., appearing as lead counsel in courts where the lawyer is not admitted) violates professional conduct rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: appearing as lead counsel in United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Utah while not admitted to practice in that Bankruptcy Court, the State of Utah, or the U.S. District Court for the District of Utah. Admission to practice in a state (Wisconsin) or registration before the USPTO does not substitute for admission to a particular court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney communications must state jurisdictional limitations — SCR 20:7.1(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lawyer communications (e.g., website biography pages) must accurately state jurisdictional limitations of the lawyer's practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to indicate on a website biography page the jurisdictions in which the lawyer is authorized to practice is a violation; website materials should clearly disclose where the attorney is licensed and where they are not admitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper handling of client trust accounts — SCR 20:1.15(e)(1)(a) and related provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules govern the maintenance and use of IOLTA/trust accounts, including the proper jurisdictional placement and permissible deposits/disbursements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of violations: maintaining a Utah IOLTA trust account while only licensed in Wisconsin; depositing a credit-card payment into the trust account in violation of SCR 20:1.15(e)(4)(e); failing to provide required written notice before disbursements from trust to business accounts per SCR 20:1.15(g)(1). Practitioners must maintain trust accounts and handle deposits/disbursements in compliance with the applicable trust-account rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to refund unearned fees upon termination — SCR 20:1.16(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon termination of representation, a lawyer must refund unearned fees without condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to refund unearned fees upon termination is a violation; the rule requires prompt, unconditional refund of unearned portions of fees when representation ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and statutory basis for USPTO disciplinary action — 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO exercises disciplinary authority over practitioners pursuant to federal statute and regulations cited as the basis for taking action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Final Order states the action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24; such statutory/regulatory citations establish jurisdiction and procedural basis for reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of disciplinary decisions — 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions affecting practitioners may be published in the Official Gazette and posted for public reading in the OED Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs the OED Director to publish a Notice of Reprimand in the Official Gazette and to ensure disciplinary decisions are posted in the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (provides URL). Compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond to Notice and Order
rubrics_metrics.description: If a respondent fails to timely file a response to a Notice and Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, the Office may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and proceed to impose the reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Here, more than forty days passed without a response, leading to the determination that no genuine issue of material fact existed and that reprimand was appropriate. Timely opposition under the enumerated regulatory defenses is the mechanism to contest reciprocal discipline.
